utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Judge Singh is away on urgent personal reasons. The proceedings will continue under Rule 15 bis. Mr. Pantelic was cross-examining. Ms. Reidy, you have something to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, it's just simply to advise Your Honours that the official translation for that list is now available, P51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I've distributed a copy to the Defence, and there are copies with the Legal Officer, so it is now available. And should Mr. Pantelic need it, the official version is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe we can have our copies. Can we have the number formally stated, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pantelic, you can proceed with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Prior to continuing, I have just short intervention in yesterday's transcript. During the cross-examination and certain line of questioning with regard to the Exhibit P40 and P40 ter, which was on the page 6560, line 21 of yesterday's session, when I asked the witness about the title in this document on the left-hand upper side, she responded that it's "Bosnia Brigade, Bosanski Samac." Maybe it was also my misunderstanding in reading this particular document, or maybe it's some kind of interpreter's error. Anyhow, I would like to clarify that, because according to my knowledge, the heading of this document is "Posavka [phoen] Brigade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we can have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just as a matter of clarification. I mean, it's not so big thing what is on the document. But still, in order to clarify the transcript, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we can have the B/C/S on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, it's a minor matter, or rather, omission. We want to rectify it. Would you please be so kind as to read the heading in the top left-hand corner of the document on the ELMO. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Posavina Brigade, Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I also add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There's no need to. We have clarified this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think the issue is clarified now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Delic, can we agree with the assertion that the institution of work obligation during wartime was within the purview of the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and its branch office in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I would really like to say something about the previous point, the document with which we closed our work yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't think that's possible now, but perhaps when you are questioned later by the Prosecutor again, you can raise that issue. I would like to come back to what I have.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to insist. Perhaps I should address myself to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was a last-minute thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can go ahead and say what she wants to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My testimony about the document which was presented to me yesterday was not my final word about the entirety of the document. My last sentence read: "I could agree with the contents." That part of the testimony regarding contents has been misunderstood as referring to the contents of the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Pantelic, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Frankly, Your Honours, I didn't understand this explanation. I don't know which document we are speaking or what it is about, but probably my learned friends in redirect can clarify all these issues. I'm not -- I don't have any intention to go to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my first question was: Can we agree with the assertion that during the state of war, the institution of work obligation was in the purview of the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska and its branch office in Bosanski Samac? Yes, no, or I don't know?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the requisition of your husband's car, and you presented us with evidence which has been admitted here as P49.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I would like this exhibit, P49, to be put in front of the witness and also on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, you mentioned that a certain person, a soldier, Stojan Blagojevic, came to you on a certain occasion and requisitioned your car against this piece of paper; correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether this person, Stojan Blagojevic, is one of suspicious character with a criminal record? Do you know anything like that?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After this event about -- after the requisitioning of your vehicle, did you learn what kind of person Stojan Blagojevic was? Did you make inquiries around town?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not -- I did not find out anything distinctive about his character or behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at this document now. I think we need to clarify certain points to the Trial Chamber. First of all, will we agree that this word in the first paragraph, "temporary-permanent use." Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Shall we explain to the Trial Chamber that in our practice, in the practice of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in such documents and in similar documents, it is usual to include two alternatives and then cross out the option which does not apply to this -- to this specific case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, I think now that Mr. Pantelic himself is testifying from the bench. Because this question about whether or not this could assist the Trial Chamber, on the use of permanent, temporary, what it meant in the content of this document, et cetera, was posed specifically in a question from the bench, and the witness testified on that. Mr. Pantelic is now trying to put forward his evidence on the record, testifying from the bench, when this has already been addressed and the witness has made clear that she doesn't know anything about it in the context of this document. And it was a question from the bench. So I'd object to Mr. Pantelic now trying to get around that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, the objection is sustained. What you can do, if you have any other instructions on the document, is to bring them up during the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. My idea was, Your Honour, just to clarify, the form of the document, which might be of importance for this Trial Chamber to follow. But I will proceed, of course. Mr. Usher you can sit. I don't need your assistance, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the course of your experience of contacts with official institutions, you would see two options in such documents, and the one which stands out to be unnecessary is usually crossed out; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this person, Stojan Blagojevic, acted in an unauthorised manner on behalf of the Crisis Staff in requisitioning your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he came on official business to my house or he did so of his own accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he show you his ID, his papers? Did he show you a document authorising him to do anything when he came in?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please read the last paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Just move the document on the ELMO, please, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last paragraph, please. Please read it.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The reimbursement for temporary use of assets or requisitioned and expended goods shall be calculated and payment made -- " It's difficult to read, because it's partially covered by the stamp -- "after the -- on the basis of authentic documentation." I can't read what's under the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness says because of the stamp, she's unable to read the last part. But it's a matter you can read yourself to her and then you can proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So "this reimbursement shall be calculated after the termination of the state of war based on authentic documents," isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can suppose that this is what it says, "based on authentic documentation."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are an economist, and you are familiar with the doctrine and theory of your science and profession that during a state of war, military authorities may requisition certain assets, with the proviso that they reimburse owners after this state of war is terminated.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read any documents of that kind. I can only assume one way or another, but I can't confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that the Dayton Peace Accords envisaged the return and reimbursement of property to all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not a question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you personally familiar with the fact that you have the right to approach the authorities of Republika Srpska asking for compensation for the use of your property?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody addressed me personally on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think there's a misunderstanding here. It's not the authorities who are supposed to contact you. I was asking, did you contact the authorities with the objective of obtaining compensation, a refund, for the use of your property? Did you take any steps in that direction?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as this vehicle is concerned, if we are talking about the requisitioning of our personal car, of our private car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I wonder whether you could clarify with the witness, although I believe she did mention this in examination-in-chief, but maybe you could clarify once again on this issue of the document in front of us saying that the claimant would have to provide authentic documentation as to ownership and so on and so forth. Could you clarify with the witness as to when the car was requisitioned, you know, was the logbook of the car and other documentation probably to do with insurance and -- you know, whatever a car owner has, were those documents also taken away when the car was taken away, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You are reading my mind. That was one of my next questions. But still -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: That's giving me something extra to know that I can read your mind, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understood you correctly, you did not claim compensation for your car. Have you claimed any other type of reimbursement for anything else from the authorities?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking here only about the requisitioning of the car and the document about that. I object to being asked questions about anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, this is a proper question which you should answer, and please do answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Pantelic, but if you could ask this witness what I suggested, and you said I was reading your mind about, as to the documents re: the car, which seem to be necessary in Exhibit P49 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with you, Your Honours. But still I would like to establish the personal attitude of this witness with regard and towards the officials. I mean, as an order anywhere --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we can hear the interpreters chatting. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please reply whether you had applied for restitution or compensation of any property. Did you initiate any proceedings?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did your husband do it?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he should be the one to testify about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss or make contacts with any lawyer about initiating such issues?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The property that I had in my marriage is all in my husband's name, so I could not really get into any activities regarding that property, because it wasn't in my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Specifically about your car, did you get in contact with any lawyer in Bosnia and Herzegovina, for him to make representations on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because for that, you required to have certain documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, I hope that you would agree with me that the documents that you need in order to do this is precisely this document that you have in your possession. That is the document that you'll require; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these legal rules to such an extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, these are not legal relations or rules, Mrs. Delic. When a body, in this case, a municipal body of Bosanski Samac, the Crisis Staff, for the needs of the state of war, et cetera, as you see at the top of the document -- so if the municipal organ, which is part of the authority, states that they will compensate you for the use and that at that point, it was taking the car documents, the traffic permit, the car itself, and in return was issuing you with an appropriate document, of which you possess the original, that means that you, with the documents that you possess or the document that you possess, could ask for the restitution or the return of that vehicle or your property. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is so, then I do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I waited to see where Mr. Pantelic would end up with this, but he's, you know -- the witness has said, "I don't know these legal rules to such an extent." He then tells her, "This is the case, this is it," putting his interpretation of the document on it when the witness says she doesn't know the legal rules. And again, I think this is an improper question. If that is an interpretation he wishes to put forth for the Defence case, then he does it at the appropriate time and not ask the witness who said she didn't know the legal rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, you've understood the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honour pleases, may I just add something to what Ms. Reidy said in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: One wonders as to the usefulness of this line of cross-examination, because if the -- I'm only guessing here, of course. But if the case for Dr. Blagoje Simic is that this is a forgery; it's nonsense; it's a piece of paper that was produced by a thug with a gun in order to steal a car. Then all of this is completely unnecessary cross-examination. I just wanted to add that. It may assist Mr. Pantelic in whether he wanted to pursue this line of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I would agree with you, Mr. Di Fazio. And also the witness has already said that she didn't make any claims. The car was registered in her husband's name. So I think maybe that is sufficient for you to understand that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree that it is rather a legal matter, so we can discuss that in our legal submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One example, Mrs. Delic. For example, before 1992, when you were changing your personal ID documents, a passport, your identify card, before 1992 in Bosanski Samac, did the appropriate body issue you with a kind of receipt that you had given them these documents?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember whether they did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, you can take these exhibits, please, and we can proceed with the other lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Delic, now we will talk about the curfew which you took -- regarding which topic you provided certain answers during the questioning from the Prosecution. I will remind you that you said that you heard on the radio that the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac had imposed a curfew; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My first question is whether you would agree with me that in a state of war, police and military bodies can impose a curfew?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said, amongst other thing, page transcript 6405, lines 21 to 24, that the curfew was imposed from 9.00 p.m. to 6.00 a.m., and that also there was an order to darken all the windows. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In any case, all the lights had to be turned off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that if there -- the reason for having to turn out the lights and to darken all the windows was the fact that the town was in danger of being shelled?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I cannot answer with "yes" or "no." I can't give my answer with just "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Bosanski Samac, until September 1992, did you perhaps hear or were present during shelling of the town, when shells were falling on the town?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. May I add a sentence here, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness add the sentence. Can the witness add the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I didn't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Go ahead. Her Honour Judge Mumba has given you her permission.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Citizens like myself, those who did not have equal rights at that time and equal duties in the newly established authority in power, were used as a sort of defence from possible shelling at that time, bombing, et cetera. We were there as kinds of hostages, as shields. I don't know if my opinion is perhaps wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, if this is a cross-examination, I think that I'm entitled as Defence counsel to follow the principles of cross-examination, otherwise the witness will expand certain stories, give personal opinions which are not related to my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If the Bench allows the witness to say what she says she wants to say and it doesn't make sense to you, you simply ignore it. You go ahead with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will have no consequence on your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But maybe, Your Honour, this kind of statement will put me in a situation to put another question, and then the cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Those are not matters you have to ask for permission. You know what your client's defence is. Yes, so you go ahead with cross-examination which will assist your client's case. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender it into evidence one document which was previously disclosed by one of my colleagues to the learned friend from the Prosecution. I believe it's 98, or 99, something like that. In the meantime, we obtained official translation of this document, and the document is actually the order of the Ministry of Interior, police station Bosanski Samac, with regard to the curfew and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's dated ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dated 17th of April, 1992. And I hope that my learned friends will confirm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Did it have a court number? You said it was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I would like for my learned friends to confirm that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can assist by getting the document from you, Mr. Pantelic, and showing it to the Prosecution so they can easily look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For the record, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I can confirm that the Prosecution had received this from Defence counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric, and we had also received an English translation from Mr. Pantelic, I believe, yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And what is the position of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And we have no objection to it being entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be D28/1, D28/1 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, could you please put the B/C/S version in front of -- yes, in front of the witness and then the English translation on the ELMO. Thank you. Could you zoom it more, to see the last part where is the signature? Excellent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Delic, could you please read the heading of this document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bosanski Samac public security services centre. Number: 01-10/92. Date: 17th of April, 1992." Should I read until the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. This is enough. Could you now read to yourself the document. You don't have to read it out aloud. Just acquaint yourself with the contents of the document, because I wanted to ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please read who signed this document. Could you please state the function of the person who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we will agree that this is the chief of police, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If that is the same thing, then very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Does it state anywhere in this order, or is there a provision in this order which imposes the curfew only for the non-Serb population, or does this order apply to all citizens of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I state in my statement that this was only for non-Serb -- applicable only to non-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Counsel has put a question to you in relation to the contents of this order which you have read. So just answer the question as it is put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. No, it's a general order applicable to all citizens in order to protect the order of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The -- no particular ethnicity is being singled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the document was not issued,, nor signed by the Crisis Staff of Samac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think that is a fair question for this witness. All the witness can see is the signature and what is written on the document. To ask her whether it was issued on the authority of the Crisis Staff is not fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard on Radio Samac that a curfew was being imposed; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you testified here that the order on the imposition of the curfew in Samac was practically made by the Samac Crisis Staff; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But I am talking about Radio Samac. I'm not talking about an order like this, a written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is there a possibility in view of the fact that this happened in 1992 that perhaps you misheard and that perhaps it was announced on the radio that the curfew was being imposed by the chief of the police? Is it possible, since ten years have gone past since then?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I stand by what I have stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, you can take these documents to the registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be more precise about certain parts of your testimony, I would kindly ask you to look at your statement from 1995 which you provided to the Prosecution. And I would like you just to confirm some things from that statement. This is the statement that we talked about yesterday which you provided to the Prosecution in 1995. Could you please turn to the page where the last two numbers are "71." The last passage on that page I would read, and if you can agree with me, please, say whether this is in your copy of the statement and whether you said that at that time. "I don't know whether Tadic was able to help my husband. I personally think that Todorovic and the army command in Pelagicevo were in charge of the release of the prisoners. I got this perception because the other Serbs also referred to Todorovic in that way." Did you state that in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now I will read a part of your statement from 1998 which you provided to the Prosecution. Unfortunately, I don't have a copy in your native language, so that the interpreters will translate this section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If it would be of assistance, we have a B/C/S version of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And secondly, just on this, I would just like to then remind Mr. Pantelic that, yesterday, he talked about this statement being signed by the witness, and I put on the record it wasn't. And we agreed that if we ever came to discuss the statement, he would then reclarify with the witness whether what he's now reading from is a signed statement or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, this is a 1995 statement now.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: 1998, Your Honour, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now we are speaking about 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And there's no problem for the Prosecution to explore this issue in redirect. It's no problem. Whether it's signed or not, I mean the statement is a statement. Otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We have to be clear with that. It's not the Prosecutor's notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, what is it, according to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's a statement that the witness gave, but it's not a signed statement. The one from 1995 is signed. The one from 1998 is not signed. And Mr. Pantelic put on the record yesterday that both the statements were signed without -- so that's what I'd like to clarify. And we said that only if we dealt with that document could we -- would we raise the issue and address it now in this context, which is why I make the intervention. So our statement is it's a statement she gave but it's a not-signed statement, just so it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But it's a statement that was recorded by an investigator of the Prosecution's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, of course, remind you that you gave this statement on the 20th of May, 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And there is a paragraph here which says: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ..."To the best of my knowledge and recollection." You remember this -- they asked you whether you gave this statement under coercion or under duress. You said no; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. -- Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe we can get a copy for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I have a copy. I don't know whether Mr. Pantelic would like a copy of the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't need. I have English translation. You can put the copy in front of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And also to complete the record, the paragraph which

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC READ OUT
utterances.text: "To the best of my knowledge and recollection," et cetera, it's not signed. That paragraph is, of course, in the format; it's in the statement in the sense that it's a formality pro forma, but the witness has not signed anything after that, that statement which Mr. Pantelic read out. Just in case the Trial Chamber might think that her signature exists after the statement he put on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's just -- it's just an anomaly that a statement recorded from a witness by a Prosecutor's investigator is not signed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It depends on the statement. Often they're taken back and then revised and read back to the witness. Other times, the investigator makes the notes and they're not signed. It really depends on the -- often the second statement isn't signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is rather, Your Honour, a matter of diligence. For example, if the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... was signed, I don't see why the witness statement from 1998 wasn't signed. But that's my opinion. It's not important

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic -- no, no, you go ahead with the cross-examination. It's for the Trial Chamber to draw conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May I assist just on this issue, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There are two statements: One is taken in 1995 and the other one is taken in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The statement in 1995 has been signed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: She has acknowledged it as her statement, and we can see that in the acknowledgment section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Also, the interpreter has signed that she interpreted the statement. So you can tell immediately that it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have no problem with 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. It's just that Mr. Pantelic is now going to the statement of 1998 and assuming that it is her statement, and we just don't know. We don't know if it's a summary of the interpreter's notes or whether it's something that was read back to her and that she --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But those are matters which the Prosecution should have state -- should be able to state, according to their position, according to the position of the Prosecution. This statement -- you say what your position is about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because you know how it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You should know. And you are the people who gave it to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Well, our position is this: There is nothing to indicate that this is her statement. She has not signed it. It says her statement -- that it's her name on the document. It's got the date. It's interview, the name of the interviewers, and so on and so forth. But it stands in total contrast to that of 1995. Now, it may be that if the witness is asked, look, did you -- "Was it read back to you?" She might be say, "Yes, it was read back to me, I understood every single word, I acknowledge it as mine completely." But we just don't know at this stage. Now, if the Chamber asks me that we should know what the position is, well, I could find out. I could go to the interviewer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. You see, Mr. Di Fazio, the problem is counsel is cross-examining on a statement which was handed to him as a statement made by the witness. If you are -- if you are contesting that, then you say so. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not contesting that. I'm not contesting that. I'm saying I don't know. I don't know. Because in 1995, you can tell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Mr. Di Fazio, we are through with 1995. It is the status of the statement recorded in 1998 which is causing a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let counsel go ahead with cross-examination. The re-examination can be done. The submissions will be made at the right time. Mr. Pantelic, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just to help my friends, this witness has answered to this question. I asked her whether it was your statement, did you say that, and whether it was read to you. She said yes. No problem with me. You can check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Delic, will you please so kind as to find the fifth or sixth paragraph on the last page. It concerns the same event with Tadic. In your statement, the English version bears the number 67006711.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The ERN number is 00 -- 00611647.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Later I used to come to the Red Cross premises to ask about the exchange. I had to contact Miroslav Tadic all the time in order to be exchanged. I would like to mention that he often used the words "this arrangement does not include Dragan," and he would also say that the lists had gone to Pelagicevo, meaning that someone in Pelagicevo was making the decision. They would not allow Dragan's name to be put on the list, because he was a Muslim." [Interpretation] You did say this to the Prosecution in 1998?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. But that was from the words of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that electricity supply in 1992 was made difficult or impossible due to sabotage actions carried out on transmission lines in the surrounding area; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the supply of electricity to Samac was cut off by the centre for distribution of electricity in -- under the control of the Muslims; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me if I were to say that during the state of war, many public utility services, such as electricity supply, telephone communications, water supply, et cetera, work under extraordinary and difficult conditions due to the state of war?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the telephone communication is an exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But everything is more difficult during the war.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether at that time it was the case only with parts or the entirety. I was not familiar with details of electricity supply or other public utilities and their situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you did testify that in certain neighbourhoods of the town, for longer stretches of time, there was no electricity at all; right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you, as a well-educated person who has experience and ability in assessing the situation, do you believe it is normal when -- for power cuts to exist during wartime, or do you think everything should run just as normal, just as always?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I didn't think so, that this is the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about Samac and telephone lines. In wartime in Samac, do you believe it was quite normal for problems to exist with telephone communication?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question with "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Answer as you like.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did experience problems during the war in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you have problems with your telephone before 1992?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did it happen at least once before 1992 that your personal -- your private telephone line was cut off?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At least not for more than an hour, and it was a minor dysfunction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So when your telephone isn't working, you contact the telephone service and ask for it to be repaired; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you told this Court that in 1992, when your telephone wasn't working, you didn't call the operator and ask for your telephone to be repaired. Why?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I knew that all my friends and neighbours of non-Serbian ethnicity also had dead telephones. I didn't know who to contact, and I didn't know if I should. And out of fear, I didn't dare to contact anyone. I was cut off from the social and economic life of the new regime, and that's how I felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us assume that your theory is correct.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate it if you would agree that it is completely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please wait for me to finish my question. Let us assume that your theory is correct. Were you aware of the fact that military and police security services, due to the suspicion that hostile elements are guiding their shelling equipment at Samac, are cutting off telephones to prevent communication with the enemy? Did you have any such knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You spoke about a tragic event concerning the isolation of non-Serbian women and children at the stadium in Crkvina near Samac.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention the stadium. I don't know exactly where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or was it Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From speaking to the women who had been taken away, I know that some of them had been in Crkvina. But I didn't learn any details about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And when was that approximately in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been the 12th of May or -- mid-May. Sometime between the 10th and the 13th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Serb refugees from the surrounding villages were expelled by Croats and arrived in Samac precisely in mid-May; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was able to spot a large group of newly arrived neighbours in Bosanski Samac. They were moving into houses and apartments owned by non-Serbian citizens who had previously been taken away to camps -- or to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in that interval, there were several thousand Serbs who were detained in surrounding villages in the area of Samac, detained by the Croatian Defence counsel, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no evidence to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, that type of evidence, whether or not the Serbs were expelled from anywhere or detained from anywhere, does not provide a defence for the charges against your client. Those are matters, I think, for the Prosecutor's office to take on and deal with and prosecute the people responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may pose certain questions and you will see the line -- the logic line of the events in Samac, with regard to this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Of course Your Honour is absolutely correct. But he says, "if I pursue this line." The witness has said she has no information and no knowledge. So how can he pursue anything with a witness who doesn't know any of the things that he is alleging happened? He's put a number of allegations, none of which have been confirmed by any knowledge, personal knowledge, of this witness, so I really can't see how he can continue to pursue down this, except for what you said, having it put on the record some form of defence which doesn't actually have value in the jurisprudence of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The objection is sustained, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, are you familiar with the incident in which a large number of Serbian refugees in Samac threatened in the middle of May that they would lynch the non-Serbian population of Samac because they and their families are targeted and subjected to horrors by Croats?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that fact. I didn't hear anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about an event when a large number of Serbian refugees gathered in the centre of the town and made a protest rally against the non-Serbian population in Samac. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that military and political authorities, with the view to protect the citizenry, decided that a large number of non-Serbian population should be moved to Crkvina to relieve the tension?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But in your testimony, you did say that after a certain time, women started coming back from Crkvina to Samac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that some of them went to be exchanged and others came back. Not always to their own homes that -- at that. I learned about it from one person who did come back to her own apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Regarding the work obligation in Bosanski Samac, are you familiar with the fact that the director of an enterprise decides about employment in that enterprise?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the institution. I assume that it was like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that your husband's brother was on work obligation.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he a military conscript?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go into that. I would not wish to testify about whether he was or wasn't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that if somebody who is mobilised as not going to the army must carry out certain work obligations? Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, I am almost at the end of my cross-examination. And I must tell you that while talking with my client, I obtained the following information: The Crisis Staff never made the orders that you mentioned regarding curfew; the Crisis Staff never made any decisions banning the gathering of three or more persons that you mentioned; the Crisis Staff had no role in any of the things that you talked about. And I would now ask you whether -- after these proceedings, either to correct your position or state that you did not talk about the Crisis Staff or that your recollection of the activities of the Crisis Staff was not really very good.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I respond to that right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made my statements according to the best of my recollection and knowledge, and I have no intention of changing what I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Delic, for your assistance before this Trial Chamber, and thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. I would also like to insist, I personally as a witness, if I may address the Honourable Judges one more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can say what you want, Mrs. Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would just like to recall the document which yesterday in one minute before 6.00 was resolved as a topic for question and answer. What I said regarding that document remained unclear to me. I don't know whether this was translated in English the way that I said it, but I think that while I was talking about that document and my stance regarding that document were not identical. Now I am talking about the translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which document is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the decree or order for bidding the gathering of more than two Muslims or Croats and so on. I don't remember the document number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Ms. Reidy can take that up in re-examination if it's important for the Prosecution. Yes, you can go ahead with re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, I'll address it as a matter of concern. But I would just like to start off the re-examination by allowing you to answer the question which Judge Williams put to you that Mr. Pantelic, in fact, didn't. So if you recall, Judge Williams had asked about documentation, possibly I think she meant permits, logbook, that sort of documentation, which was normally attached to ownership of a car. What happened to that documentation when the car was taken away?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the documents relating to the car were together with the car's documents, and they were in the -- they were in the car. Everything that was in the car, all the documentation were taken away. It was all in the glove compartment. So I don't know exactly which documents they were, but all the documents regarding the car were there, and they were all taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, is that enough clarification on that matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, I will continue just now to pick up matters that Mr. Pantelic raised in his cross, since I started there. And perhaps I'll start again with this document that concerns you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For the record, it's P40.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now you testified yesterday that the contents of that document, the prohibition, was the same contents as what you had -- what you had seen. Can I ask you, on the 27th of June, when your car was taken, by that time -- so prior to the 27th of June -- had you already seen on a public poster or something like that an order saying that there should be a -- there should be no gathering of two or more non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't state the exact date, but the month of August was on the document. I don't know the exact date when it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mrs. Delic. I'm not asking you to talk about the document, which speaks for itself. And you're correct; it's August. Just, you talked about the contents of it. And I want to know whether you knew the contents of that order. So were you aware of a prohibition on the gathering of non-Serbs before, for example, the 27th of June? I know you don't know when exactly you first heard it, but by the time your car was taken, were you already aware there was a prohibition on the gathering of non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 27th of June. It was -- in any case, in the month of July, I already was informed about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I -- and to clarify, did you know this information from reading, like, a public poster, a sign? Or was it an order, an issue, put through your door?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't issued per person, but these were all public posters.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask if the witness could be given a copy of her statement from 1995 which is signed and Mr. Pantelic had asked her a number of questions about it. I have a copy here. For the record, the witness is being provided with the B/C/S version of the statement which Mr. Pantelic based his cross-examination on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, could I ask you to turn to the page which Mr. Pantelic asked you about. I think it was page 6, or with the ERN in the top corner ending in "68." Have you got to that page? In the bottom right-hand corner, it will say "6," and the top will have the last two digits "68." Okay. Can I ask you to look at the fourth paragraph from the bottom of that. And does the second sentence -- or perhaps you could read out the second sentence of that -- the fourth paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I saw posters" -- is that the passage?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I saw posters in public places and institutions in which Serbs forbade the gathering of Muslims and members of other ethnicities in public places."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I now ask you -- Mr. Pantelic had then turned to the next page, page 7, or the one in the top-hand corner with a "69" in it. And he'd asked you to, I think, read the fourth -- anyway, one of those paragraphs from the B/C/S. And then he didn't ask you to continue. So I'd ask you to go to the fourth paragraph from the bottom of the statement in B/C/S. And then if you could perhaps read it out and tell me whether or not you confirm that that's also part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The orders were issued by the Crisis Staff and the President of the Serb Assembly, Blagoje Simic. They were announced on posters posted in public places, and over the radio. The posters were signed, not originally. And they also bore the stamp with the 4-S logo." And I abide by what I have stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And can I confirm, this is something that you said in 1995, just three years after the event and not just here in the courtroom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned in the paragraph you just read a stamp with 4 C's on it. Is that the same stamp that you described seeing at the bottom of the document you were provided with when your car was taken away?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness just to be provided with two exhibits, the Exhibit P49 and the Exhibit D28/1. And sorry, in both cases, could the witness be shown the ter versions, the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, could I ask you to look at both of those documents in front of you and ask whether the stamp on both of those are the stamps -- the sort of stamp you're referring to as seeing in these public posters and that in 1992 in Samac.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They're the same stamps.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And your understanding of the stamps is what, that this was from the official authorities at the time? Or what did that stamp mean to the people in Samac at the time when they saw that on something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. Objection. It's calling for speculation, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes, what did the people in Samac at the time they saw that, what did they think? Okay. Maybe just the witness, as to what she thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to testify about other people's impression, I'm sorry. But for you, you said this was the stamp you saw on orders. What Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 6602 to 6608. did it mean to you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, it meant that this was the stamp of the official authorities, the new Serb municipality or the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted to raise with those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If the usher would like to assist me and just take them back from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, you were asked about whether a document put in front of you by Mr. Pantelic made any reference to the curfew only being applicable to any particular ethnic group or only to non-Serbs, and you confirmed that the document in front of you didn't specify it. Do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, when you're asking the witness "a document put in front of you," can you -- at the end of your question, can you say "I'm referring to exhibit number or identification number," please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I was referring on that occasion to the Exhibit D28/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, you said your knowledge of the curfew came from the radio and not from that document. But -- sorry. And then my question is: Did you experience from your observation of the curfew and the way it was imposed that different members of different groups were expected to -- could obey it or were free to disobey it if they chose?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could understand that, based on the events which followed after I found out about this announcement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm just objecting on speculation, really just the form of the question. This witness obviously can testify to what it meant to her from her observation. But when the questions are broad, trying to elicit some general impression, I just think that's improper and I think it can be remedied by reformulating the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm happy to reformulate. I certainly don't want the witness to speculate. I had thought I had asked specifically from her experience and her observation when she was in Samac, her personal knowledge. How was the curfew actually observed and enforced from her personal experience.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So that's the question, Mrs. Delic, from your personal experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. From her personal experience. That's proper. You can go ahead, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I noticed was the fact that despite the curfew, after the set hour, 9.00 p.m., some people were moving on the streets. I could recognise a few of my neighbours who went to visit one another in the evening hours, and then they would come back home normally after 21 hours. Q.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Here it says that a few of your neighbours went to visit one another. They would normally come back after 21 hours. Were those neighbours of Serb ethnicity, of non-Serb ethnicity, or were they both?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were Serb families. It's no secret that the Dujmusic family, the Todorovic family, the Krstanovic family, all lived in my neighbourhood, and they socialised, they visited one another. So I could see some members of those families who were moving around after the curfew.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn now to questions that were posed about rumours you'd heard concerning the background of your husband's arrest. Mr. Pantelic brought up the fact that you'd heard that he could be on a list of suspicious persons, that someone allegedly fired from your house. Did anybody fire from your house?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think I didn't bring up the fact. I just put the statement, her statement, in front of her. I just -- so in that terms, you can, my dear friend, reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The question is okay. The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, you can answer. Did anyone fire from your house?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever fired from the apartment where I lived -- where I used to live. I apologise. Where I used to live at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did your husband have a weapon which he could have fired from?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not have a weapon. And of course, all of those who did have a weapon had to have a permit in order to carry that weapon or to purchase a weapon. These -- we did not have that kind of permit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Then, as you had said in your statement and it was raised by Mr. Pantelic, you heard another reason, that maybe your husband -- they were investigating whether your husband had signed any compromising documents in the Mebos factory about financing the purchasing of weapons. And again, did your husband, to the best of your knowledge, sign any compromising documents about financing the purchase of weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's improper question. How she could know what her husband signed or not? I mean, it's a question for her husband, anyway. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Some couples exchange information. Maybe the husband could have told her. And the question was "to the best of your knowledge," to the best of the witness's knowledge. So she can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe the question could be reformulated, whether your husband told you something about this particular event or not, did you speak with him. I mean, it's rather general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Yes. But she did add "to the best of your knowledge." That's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Ms. Delic, could you answer the question: To the best of your knowledge, did your husband ever sign any documentation, compromising documentation about the financing of purchasing of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't sign such documents. And I would like to add here to my statement that during those few days, because of rumours like that, I tried to find amongst the new leaderships or the authorised persons of the public accounting service in Bosanski Samac, and I contacted Mr. Ilija Mitrovic, who had been in the public accounting service before, and I tried to find out whether there was any information or any document in the public accounting service about this matter, and he told me that up to that time, none -- documents of that kind were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's quarter to 4.00, and that would normally be the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall have a break and continue our proceedings at 14.15 -- at 16.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. Re-examination continuing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, I just have one or two more questions on the questions put to you by Mr. Pantelic. Prior to the 17th of April, 1992, did you have any hesitation in approaching the official authorities if you had a problem, for example, with your telephone, or if somebody had -- you know, you were entitled to compensation? Would you have hesitated to go to the authorities before the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nor did I have any problems with having my claims or requests satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You've testified that you didn't go to the telephone company or you didn't pursue a number of matters with official authorities. Was there such a dramatic change after the 17th of April that you no longer -- I mean, was it usual that you wouldn't have continued as you had before the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seemed a normal conclusion to make for me, from my point of view, because I was no longer welcome at my work and I was excluded from the social and economic life of the community under the new regime, and I therefore understood that I no longer had the opportunity to have any of my claims or requests met through normal official channels.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic asked you a lot about how difficult war conditions are, and in general, the problems of running things during wartime. And he began his questioning by asking you whether or not it was the common fate of all the inhabitants of the town. And you said that you did not all share the same. Can I ask you, in your personal experience and based on your -- the fact that you were a non-Serb living in Bosanski Samac in April 1992, did you experience discrimination after the 17th of April, 1992, because you were a non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for a legal conclusion. "Discrimination," that's a legal term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Partly upheld. Ms. Reidy, you can rephrase the question, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Ms. Delic, were you treated differently as a non-Serb in Bosanski Samac after the 17th of April, 1992, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could conclude that with certainty from the way I was living, and I have to say this again, from the way I was included, or rather, excluded from the economic life of my town, the work duties, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it would be -- it will be more helpful to ask if she gives us a few more details in what way she was excluded, in what way she was treated differently, and who was being treated as usual.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would you help us in that in filling in some details.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say that I was not included in the social and economic life under the new regime, I mean to say that I simply felt as if I didn't exist. And there was an awareness in me that if a person is not invited to work even in a wartime economy, when one has to make a special effort to make ends meet, and after all, I was alone with two children living in my flat from the 17th of April to the 4th of September. And I have already stated in my testimony which of my colleagues from the school continued to work as teachers or administrators. So that's all I would have to say about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So could you tell us, the people you were being treated differently from, who were they exactly? Were they -- which population group were they? Were they Serb?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, citizens of Serb ethnicity had rights. I have already quoted examples of saleswomen. And I said that Serb -- non-Serb saleswomen were left out at one point, were relieved, whereas Serb saleswomen continued in their jobs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So one example where you experienced being treated differently was with relation to continuing to work as a teacher. Are there any other examples you could give the Chamber as to how you were excluded or treated differently from people of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reading decisions such as the decision banning socialising or gathering of non-Serbs, I clearly realised my new status in that newly established Serbian community.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll leave that there and move on to the cross-examination of Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Ms. Baen asked you specifically about the issue of visits to the primary school. And at one stage, you began to relate an anecdote or an incident about how you tried to go to the primary school and then you used the word, you had to "abort" the attempt. And you weren't allowed to give that example. But I'd like you now to say -- to fill us in. Could you please continue what you wanted to say about that time you tried to see your husband.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said that on that day, I went to that school, together with my children, thinking that I would be able to arrange for my children to see their father, at least for a few moments. They were overjoyed, of course. I took a small lunch bag, as usual, and a bag with fresh, clean laundry, a change of clothes, and we were standing at the entrance to the building. At the same time, a car approached, driven by a police officer, Savo Cancarevic. I was able to recognise him, and I knew that he worked as a policeman in town even before the war. He was yelling, "What is this woman doing here? Who allowed her to be here? I'll shoot." I just told my children to run ahead and leave the courtyard. I didn't want to run myself though. I just tried to contain my pride and started walking away slowly. That, again, once again, reminded me of my status in that town and my current way of living.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So based on that, I take it that these visits were not officially sanctioned visits in any sense of a prison visit. They were simply the opportunities you took to get a glimpse of your husband or tried to get him through something. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I would also like to add that sometimes my attempts to see him did not succeed also because he was unable to get up and walk up to the door because he had been beaten up the night before and he was unable to move the next day, or a couple of days even. Sometimes I could only receive a bag of dirty laundry through the guard, and this laundry had bloodstains on it. And that -- in that way, I was able to know what was going on inside. It was like a message from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the guard ever tell you that he was unable to come to you, or he just simply told you that you wouldn't be allowed to see your husband that day and gave you these bloodstained clothes?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would just say, "Here. This is for you." No explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever hear singing when you went to try to see your husband?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes in the evening or late at night -- my house wasn't far away from the school, and in the summertime, you could hear what was going on; not clearly perhaps, but you could hear singing from that direction. The songs were Serb nationalist songs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And my last question on this point is: Do you know whether the guards who were minding it had any instructions about working certain shifts or working any routine?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn now to the examination by counsel for Mr. Tadic. Did Mr. Tadic warn you to hide your money when you went on the bus because it might be taken from you? Did he give you that warning?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about that, and I think I said in my statement that I hadn't heard anything to that effect from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked about the name of this organisation who was arranging exchanges, and you called it the Serbian Red Cross. And who told you that it was now called the "Serb Red Cross," and not the "Bosanski Samac Municipal Red Cross"?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have no proof with me, but I'm certain that there existed emblems and signs with the lettering "Serbian Red Cross." I am certain that such signs existed in Bosanski Samac at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
