utterances.text: You were asked about the building that the Serbian Red Cross was in, and you were asked about whether or not they flew the sign of the Red Cross over it. And I want to know, at that building, did you see armed personnel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question that I -- the questions that I asked are not properly quoted by Ms. Reidy. I asked questions about the headquarters of the Red Cross, not the Serbian Red Cross, so I would appreciate it if the Prosecutor would pay attention to that when re-examining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, I think you can check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- Mr. Krgovic is absolutely right. He himself, I think, called it the Bosanski Samac conference of the Red Cross. And I didn't mean to imply that he had called it the Serbian Red Cross. The witness refers to this institution as the Serbian Red Cross. And I was saying that she was asked questions about the building where that was. So I'm sorry if it's misleading that Mr. Krgovic had put it that way, then I stand corrected. It was asked about the building -- it was referred to as a building, "the office of the Red Cross were in a home for retired people."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So Mrs. Delic, I'll rephrase the question, and the tenor of the question remains the same. You were asked about the building where Mr. Krgovic calls it the Red Cross was -- the offices of the Red Cross were, and about the flag flying. And my question is, in the place where the flag was flying, did you also see military people or armed people?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the premises of the Red Cross, whichever one of them we are talking about. I visited offices of the Red Cross located in the home for retired people. At that time, Mr. Tadic owned weapons himself when he was in those offices, and I think it says somewhere in my statement that his gun was lying on the desk. I don't know anything about the others. At that time I didn't have any contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Tadic in a military -- wearing a military uniform or civilian clothes when you went to see him in the offices?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time he was in a military uniform, a camouflage military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, I think for the clarity of the record, you do say "most of the time." Does that mean that sometimes he wasn't?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that on the day of the exchange, he wasn't wearing his uniform. I clearly remember that he was wearing a summer or a light shirt. In any case, it was civilian clothing. But during my visits, he was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the end of my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Delic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. It's now over. You can go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has nothing to do with the witness. I just think maybe it is a good time for us, because we have received some translations, official translations of some documents that we already introduced into evidence. So maybe it is a good time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- for us to give it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. While we are waiting for the next witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, is Mr. Lazarevic asking us for -- is he going to just hand up the translations, or ask us whether or not we consent to documents that are identified going fully into evidence? I've got no problem, of course, with the translations being handed up. But as to if you want an answer from the Prosecution as to our position on these documents, then I'd need more time to look at them, go through the transcript, see why we objected in the first place and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. I'm sure Mr. Lazarevic will be able to say whether or not the documents were given an ID number because of lack of translation or for some other reason. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are documents that already have number. They were identified just for identification. So they have ID numbers. English translation have been provided to the Office of the Prosecutor, to their case manager, a couple of days ago. I was just waiting for a proper moment, not to interrupt anything here in the -- at the Bench. And so the Prosecutor is fully aware of the content of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But anyhow, the translation that we have received of some -- these are translation of some portions, so of constitution, of law, of All People's Defence, and things like that. So I don't believe that there will be any dispute in these regards. But of course, if the Prosecutor insists -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Just give us document by document, and the ID numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First is number D11/4 ID. So far it was marked ter, so this is, I believe, D11/4 ID. Then D12/4 and D13/4, these three documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in the meantime, Your Honours, following our standard procedure with regard to the position of the Defence prior to a new witness, maybe we could just make a quick swap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking the security to allow the accused persons just to swap places, in any order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: While that's occurring, may -- if Your Honours please, may I just approach the Defence bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I need to speak to Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the English translation -- okay. Maybe we can bring in the witness, and the documentation can be dealt with. Ms. Baen -- I mean, Ms. Reidy. It's Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I just wanted to advise you that I've had a quick review of those documents, 11 through to 13/4, and the Prosecution position is we have no objection at all to them being fully entered into evidence. They're straightforward translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, the Prosecution can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the witness who just walked out of court, Snjezana Delic is your wife, I believe.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: We have two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And is that a boy and a girl?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: A boy and a girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And are you and your family currently residing in a nearby European country, not being Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's your current occupation, the occupation you have as we speak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I work in a printing shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want to know a bit more about your past. Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 15th of July, 1952 in Doboj, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber where you went to school. I'm talking about both elementary school and your high school, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I finished elementary and secondary school in Bosanski Samac, and I received a degree in machine engineering in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Up until April of 1992, had you lived most of your life in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And by that stage, that is, April of 1992, you, I think, already had -- both your children had already been born and you were living there with your wife; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How old were your kids in 1992? Can you give us an idea, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: My daughter was ten and my son was seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where were you working in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I worked at the Mebos factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what sort of job were you performing there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I was the president of the managing board.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In addition to high school education, did you attain some sort of university education?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I finished the faculty of mechanical engineering in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did that background assist you in working at Mebos?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: As a citizen of the former Yugoslavia, did you perform military service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber when you performed it, how long you performed it for, if you specialised in anything, and where you performed it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I served in the military in 1979. I was in Sombor and Bihac for a year, and I completed special training for a signalman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In plainer English, would that be basically radio operating, the use of radio sets in the military setting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I also want you to tell the Chamber if you have had any affiliations or associations with any political parties. And I'm really speaking about the period of time leading up to April of 1992. In fact, to clarify matters, I should expand the question. I'm really covering any political affiliations at any time in your life, but leading up to the period of time in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: As a competitor in the state sports teams, I was accepted into the Communist Party 1970. I was not an active member of the League of Communists since 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about your ceasing to be an active -- the period of time after your ceasing to be an active member of the League of Communists? Did you engage in any other political activity or join any other political parties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If asked to describe your ethnicity, how would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: My father is a Muslim; so is my mother; and so am I.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if your name, your full name, Dragan Hasana Delic, is an obviously Muslim name. In other words, would a normal citizen of the former Yugoslavia in the early 1990s, upon hearing your name, instantly recognise you as being a member of the -- or being Muslim by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: If you said "Dragan Delic," you wouldn't know immediately that I was a Muslim. If you added my father's name, son of Hasan, then you could tell that I was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber approximately when you first met him and how long you've known him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I know him from about town. And the last time I saw him was a couple of months before the aggression on Bosanski Samac, in the premises of the waterworks company, in the office of the director, Muharem Barjaktarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do I take it from your answer that you didn't have any sort of extended social or professional contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: That's true; I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Look around the room and see if you can see him. And if so, point him out.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: He is sitting over there. He has a small beard, and he's wearing a blue tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May the transcript reflect that the witness has correctly identified the defendant Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have the same questions for you that I had in respect of Mr. Blagoje Simic; in other words, how long you've known him, the sort of contact you had with him, whether it was professional or social. And after you've told us, answered those questions, could you also identify him, if you can see him in the room.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise him. Simo Zaric is sitting in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And may the transcript reflect that the witness has identified Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He hasn't answered fully how long has he known him and his social contacts, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now can we deal with the other aspect of the question, namely, how long you've known him, the sort of contact you had with him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: He's been working and living in Bosanski Samac for a number of years. I know him very well. He used to be the director of the Buducnost company. I know him well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have the same series of questions in relation to a gentleman named Mr. Tadic. Can you inform the Trial Chamber if you know that man, Mr. Miroslav Tadic, how long you've known him, the sort of contact you had with him, and if you can look around the room and see if you can identify him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I've known him for a number of years now: As my neighbour, then as a teacher of a practical subject at school. Then he opened a shop where we often shopped, me and my family. After that, he opened the AS Cafe, where I didn't used to go, but I know him very well. He's sitting at the beginning, and he is wearing a moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And may the transcript reflect that the witness has correctly identified Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honour pleases, I'm not going to deal with the identification issue of any other defendant in this case, for obvious reasons. I understand that from having spoken to Ms. Baen that the issue will be resolved, I believe -- I think to our satisfaction and the Court's satisfaction by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't need to trouble the Chamber with that issue at the moment. But I just wanted to point that out, that -- for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've said that you -- after you left the League of Communists, you didn't have any political connections. In the period of time leading up to April of 1992, did you ever attend any political rallies, political meetings, or meetings where current and important issues of the day were discussed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I attended one meeting of the local commune where the topic of opening the bridge across the Sava was discussed, opening it up to normal traffic. The bridge was closed at that point in time. The meeting was attended by Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like to get more details of this meeting. First of all, was it attended by representatives of various nationalist political parties: the SDS, SDA, and HDZ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They did attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And tell the Chamber how it was that you came to attend this particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I was very interested in opening the bridge up for traffic because my company obtained certain spare parts from Slovenia. So we were in the situation where we had to halt our production because we were not able to get our supplies of the material that we needed. Amongst other things, I heard at that meeting for the first time openly from Simo Zaric that there exists a formation called the 4th Detachment, which was part of the military forces of the JNA from Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you there. I need to get more details about the meeting itself. First of all, where was the meeting conducted? And secondly, when was the meeting conducted in relation to events of the 16th and 17th of April, 1992? If you can't give us a precise date, please give us an approximation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: This was a couple of months before the 16th and 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where was it conducted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: The meeting was held in the building they called the old pensioner's hall, which had a meeting room where the local community also held its meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I earlier asked you how you came to attend at the meeting. In fact, I was interested in how your attendance was arranged. Did you go there on your own initiative? Were you invited, or did you find yourself there through some other means?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic informed me that the topic of opening the bridge would be discussed at that meeting. And I gladly agreed to attend this meeting. Sulejman Tihic was the President of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm interested in. Is the fact that he was President of the SDA party of significance in the fact that you attended?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I attended that meeting because my company had an interest in it. I was a non-party representative, speaking on behalf of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you explain that idea to the Chamber. What does it mean to be a non-party representative but nonetheless to speak on behalf of a party?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: A non-party candidate means the following: This person is not a member of the SDA party but it's possible for that person to participate in certain meetings and, in certain circumstances, he is also expected to address the meeting or say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have any instructions from the SDA or any representative of the SDA as to any particular stance that you should adopt on any particular issue at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. And I requested at that meeting that a solution be found, that a way be found, for the bridge across the river Sava to be opened, otherwise, we would find ourselves in a situation that 500 employees of the company where I worked would lose their jobs and also lose their means of living. We were not able to continue production in these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio. That being said, the witness had said on page 57, line 7, "non-party representative, speaking on behalf of the SDA party," and then you went on to ask him what it means to speak on behalf of a party as a non-party representative. But it now appears in some of the later statements that the witness was not speaking -- was not instructed by a party. So I'm wondering whether the earlier reference on page 57 is just maybe something in the translation. So maybe -- maybe you can identify was he speaking on behalf of the SDA, or was he not speaking on behalf of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I understand Your Honour's dilemma in the evidence. I -- I'll do what I can do clarify that. I'm alive to the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the company he worked for, did he -- was it a company owned by SDA?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This business of the non-party representative of the SDA is obviously troubling the Chamber, and we want to be absolutely clear about what it means. You say that you had to go along as a non-party representative. But it appears that you didn't adopt any stance or say anything on behalf of the SDA. First of all, is that absolutely correct? You made no statement or utterances that reflected SDA policy or SDA positions or issues? If it's not correct, please tell the Chamber what the true situation is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: In the local elections, I was a non-party candidate of the SDA. I came to that meeting as a businessman in order to resolve the problem of spare parts supplies. I used the fact that I knew Mr. Sulejman Tihic, and I asked him to tell me when it would be possible to discuss the question of opening of the Sava bridge to traffic, which is what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Did you initiate the move to attend at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You also said that in local elections, that you were a non-party candidate of the SDA. First of all, did you ever stand for public office in any elections?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, doing the best you can, can you explain as clearly as you can to the Chamber what it means to be a non-party candidate of the SDA in local elections.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: There was the possibility that besides candidates of the national parties, the party proposes a certain number of non-party candidates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that it was a -- a political party could nominate candidates, notwithstanding the fact that they were not members of that party?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it could propose that they carry out certain duties within the town or in the local community.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have political sympathies with the SDA, notwithstanding the fact that you weren't actually a member?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I did not uphold or support the policies of any nationalist party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you initiate or take any moves to become what is known as a non-party candidate of the SDA, or was that done for you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Someone else, Izet Izetbegovic, asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Whether I would be willing to be a non-party candidate of the SDA, in view of the fact that many people knew me in town and that this would be good for the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you agree to this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I agreed to be a non-party candidate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the practical effect of your agreeing to do this? Did anything actually happen as a result of you agreeing to do this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: When the local elections took place, they published a list of the national parties. The SDA issued its own list, but they didn't separate the non-party candidates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Does that mean that you would have appeared on that list as an SDA member?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: After the list was published, I made a remark. And after that, there was an explanation that Perica Krstanovic was against placing non- -- against separating the non-party candidates on the lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I don't know how far you want me to pursue this topic. It's not of any great consequence of the Prosecution. I don't know if you're satisfied with how far I've taken it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can I ask you to turn your attention now to the meeting itself that you were talking about earlier. And you said that Mr. Simo Zaric spoke at that meeting. I'd like you now to tell the Chamber what exactly, as far as you can remember, he said at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: He said openly on that occasion that rumour had it in Samac that there existed a 4th Detachment. He said it was true. He said such a military formation did exist and that military formation belonged to a military unit in the town of Brcko. Then he said that he could even state the number of members of that unit, if the others were prepared to tell him the number of the police in the national parties. By that time, national parties had established their national police forces, and these national police forces existed alongside the regular police in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Did anyone else speak on that particular topic, apart from him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No, no one did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you recall if -- anything else he said, or is that the extent of your recollection of what he said on that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: He said that the 4th Detachment had been established as a military group that was to protect the town of Samac, but he didn't say from whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he asked? That is, was he asked from whom the town was to be protected?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No one asked him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, have you now told the Chamber of all that you can recall Mr. Simo Zaric saying at that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Delic, it's not beyond dispute -- sorry, it's not in dispute in this case that in the months leading up to April of 1992, there was considerable tension in the town of Bosanski Samac and that people were armed -- some people were armed. Did you possess any weapons in the period of time leading up to April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I never possessed a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever try to acquire a weapon in the time leading up to the 16th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever join any patrols that might have been operating in the town of Bosanski Samac or in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You are aware, I think, of a body called the TO, or Territorial Defence. Did you ever join that body or seek to become an active member of it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just returning now to your position at Mebos. I think you said you were the managing director. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I was chairman of the board of directors. And in addition to that, I dealt with all affairs related to technology and development.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have access to funds of the company in an uncontrolled way, that is, at your own discretion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've told the Chamber that you didn't own weapons or try to own weapons. Did you ever try to purchase weapons on behalf of anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever use Mebos funds to try and purchase weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would it have been possible for you to use Mebos funds to purchase weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: It wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Prior to the 16th of April, 1992, had anyone spoken to you or accused you of trying to purchase weapons on behalf of -- through the offices or the agency of Mebos?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did anyone else at Mebos purchase weapons in the period of time leading up to the 16th of April, 1992, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I now want you to turn your attention to the events of the night of the 16th and 17th of April, 1992, please. First of all, at the time, were you residing somewhere in the actual town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of place was it? Was it an apartment or a separate house standing by itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: It was a house with two apartments in it. It was owned by the organisation where I worked, that is, by my employer. One employee of the same company occupied the ground floor, and I occupied the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was the person who occupied the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: It was an employee of the maintenance unit, Josip Josarevic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Asim Josarevic. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So was it a two-storey building, two apartments, you're in one of them and the other fellow was down below; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like you to describe to the Chamber what you saw and heard during the night of the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. And I'm not talking about the day of the 17th. I'm talking about the night. The night.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: The night -- the night of the 17th of April, two or three hours after midnight, an explosion was heard, followed by a number of shots. And then after a while, everything went quiet. I stayed inside with my family, waiting for the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did you see in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: The next morning, a neighbour, Perica Krstanovic, knocked on my door and told me to come out immediately, to come outside. And when I did so, there was a vehicle on the other side of the street and a group of five to six men in camouflage uniforms. They beckoned me to come up to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just interrupt you there. This man Krstanovic, what ethnic background was he? And secondly, where did he work? What was the name of his employer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Perica Krstanovic is a Serb by ethnicity. He was the director of the electrical company in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please continue. You were describing the scene. You'd seen a group of men in camouflage uniforms and they beckoned to you. Did you approach them? And if so, carry on the story from there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: When I approached, the men in camouflage uniforms had their faces painted with some sort of black cream. They had black caps, and they had their arms cocked and ready to shoot. They asked me what my name was. And when I answered, they asked me, "Are you a Serb?" I said no. I said I was a Muslim. They asked me if I had any weapons inside my home. I said no. They asked me to swear to that, and I said, "I do swear." Then they said, "Swear on your mother's name." And I said, "I do swear on my mother's name."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you comment on the accent that they spoke with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: They spoke the Ekavian dialect which is spoken in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know a gentleman named Muharem Bajrektarevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he mentioned that morning on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: At that moment, Muharem Bajrektarevic was not standing outside his front door. And one of the members of the special unit asked, "Where is the man from that house?" Somebody replied that he was probably in the basement. Then that man said, "He should be told to get out of the basement immediately, because if he doesn't, we will deal with him the same way we dealt with such things in Vukovar. We'll throw a bomb." And Vukovar is in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: These men in camouflage uniforms speaking with the Ekavian dialect, were they accompanied by any local people, any local people that you recognised? Or were they apparently on their own?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you not hear my question? Shall I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: There were no locals among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the men in camouflage uniforms succeed in flushing out Mr. Barjaktarevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Later, somebody went around the back of the house and informed him that he should come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how old was this gentleman, Mr. Barjaktarevic, and secondly, of what ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: He was about 65 years old, and he is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, was there anything in the scene that you saw when you were out on the street to indicate that the resident of that house was missing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me put it this way: Was there anything that you could see that showed that the people gathered on the street did not include the resident of the house of Mr. Barjaktarevic, in other words, that he was missing, that he wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: There was nobody standing in front of his house, and that's why they reacted and asked where the man occupying that house was. I suppose that they knew in advance who lived where, in which house. And on the basis of that knowledge when they were questioning me, I think they knew what my answers would be in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's precisely the issue I'm interested in. You say that you suppose that they knew in advance who lived where. Thinking back now, is there anything that you can point to that led you to that conclusion or to that suspicion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Muslims were standing in front of their houses. And when there was nobody outside a certain house, they would react immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you see any Serbs standing outside or lined up outside their houses in the same manner that Muslims were lined up or standing outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: Only my neighbour Perica, the one who asked me to come out in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: He was standing at the gate to his garden, his yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see him questioned by the men in camouflage as to his possession of weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: They didn't question him. And judging by his behaviour, I thought he wasn't excited or surprised, or anxious. You couldn't detect any fear in him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've told us that the men asked you about whether or not you had guns, made you swear, and then asked about the elderly gentleman, Mr. Barjaktarevic. Did they eventually accept your explanation that you didn't have weapons and let you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, over the radio unit through which they communicated with other members of their unit, somebody interfered with their communication. And then this member of the special unit yelled at the person who was interfering, cursed his Ustasha mother, and said that unless he gets out of the way immediately, he will shoot everyone in the street. After that, he yelled again and said, "Listen, you all. Not a single shot must be fired from this street. If a single shot is fired, I'll have you all killed." When somebody asked, "And what happens if somebody else shoots," he answered, "You have to prevent it." Later they continued in their military vehicle and left our street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see where they went?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: When they arrived at the first intersection, one of them motioned with his hand towards a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What restaurant was that and who owned it, and what ethnic background was the person who owned it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: The restaurant was owned by Atif, Rajec. He was a Muslim and a member of the SDA. When I returned to my home --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on your account of things. I want to hear what happened as they got to the end of the street and the man pointed at Atif, Rajec's restaurant. Tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: When they reached the end of the street, people had already started going back inside their homes. And ten minutes later, we could hear an explosion. The next day, I heard from my neighbour, Barjaktarevic, that a grenade was thrown -- had been thrown on the restaurant that I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the restaurant destroyed, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: From the description I heard, the lower part of the restaurant was destroyed because it was mainly made of glass, and could not be used any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that the destruction of the restaurant was something that was reported to you and not something that you were able to observe with your own eyes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, I'm going to move on to another topic now, events of the following day. I recall what you said yesterday about the Status Conference. It's a little early by a few minutes, but it is Friday afternoon, after all, and if you would like to proceed to that now, this would be a convenient time, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, we will continue with your evidence on Monday, at 14.15 hours. You'll be led out of the courtroom for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.43 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of March, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
